text:
Filip Hronek is carrying a heavy load in Vancouver: 26.4 minutes a night, 27.3 over the last ten, and 31.2 in Monday's loss to Philadelphia. He reached 300 career points this month, and his 13 points (12 assists, eight on the power play) had BVM Sports pointing out that he sat among the league's top 15 scoring defensemen.

The production is about where it should be. His scoring rate sits inside our talent range, and one goal on 1.55 expected is a small shortfall, not a story. The harder part is defending on a team that has lost nine of ten. At five-on-five Vancouver gets 39% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and he has blocked 41 shots. Evolving-Hockey's read on last season is useful context: 1.6 wins above replacement, 41st among 215 defensemen, mostly from the power play, while playing with teammates in the bottom 6%. Watch him jump into the play: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 25% of his shots coming off the rush, against 17% for a typical defenseman.
headline: Filip Hronek is carrying Vancouver's heaviest load
